text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- The demand for temporary workers is increasing. The employment rate of temporary workers has doubled since 1989. So far in 1996, the rate has risen by 35 percent.
- House prices continue to increase. During the last year house prices have increased by 10 percent.
- State-owned power generator Statkraft signed a letter of intent to build a power plant in Indonesia. The deal is worth 3.5 billion crowns.

- A revision of Norway's national accounts shows that the country contributes less aid to developing countries as a measure of gross domestic propduct (GDP) than first thought. During the last ten years Denmark and Sweden have probably given more foreign aid than Norway.

- Nearly 50 percent of employees at the the Oslo Bourse have resigned since Kjell Froensdal took over as director in 1995. Froensdal does not reject that some of the resignations may have been due to his style of leadership.
